# svGolf: what the checker refuses, and what you can write

svGolf asks for two things about each design you submit: a Lean proof that it meets the task's trusted statement under the ls-sv
semantics, and a score from a pinned Yosys flow. The checker refuses a design or a proof when the proof and the score could be about
different circuits, or when the evidence could be forged. This document lists every refusal the checker makes, why, and what you
can write instead, then says which refusals are meant to go away and which never will.

It has two halves that are easy to confuse. **The checker's own stages** (source gate, banlist, fourstate, statement, axioms, score,
post-synthesis check) are described below stage by stage. **The language tier** (`ls-sv`, the semantics your proof is about) refuses
more constructs than the checker does; those show up as `extract` or `design` failures and are summarised near the end and listed in
full in `docs/sv-refusals.md` of the Proglib repository.

This file is generated from `docs/sv-refusals.json` of Proglib (formerly lean-surfaces) by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and is written to be
read without the rest of that repository: links to Proglib documents are given as repository paths.

## How to read this document

Every restriction has one of four states. A mark `†` means the classification is a proposal, not yet confirmed by the maintainers.

| state | meaning |
|---|---|
| `refused-now` | refused loudly today and this is the intended behaviour at this version; no future is recorded |
| `later` | refused today and intended to be ALLOWED once a stated prerequisite is met (a proof obligation, a model extension, a checker stage, a measured benefit); the row names the prerequisite and, where recorded, the plan item |
| `never` | refused by principle and not to be allowed: no meaning can be given that is the same for the proof (ls-sv / slang) and the score (Yosys netlist), or it is not synthesizable hardware, or it would let the proved design differ from the scored one; the row names the principle |
| `refused-pending` | decided and in flight, not yet in the code (transitional): the row names the decision; the completeness check allows its tag to be absent and warns once it appears |

The `never` rows rest on these principles:

| principle | statement |
|---|---|
| `P-SAME-PROGRAM` | Proof and score read ONE program: a construct the two frontends (slang for the proof, Yosys for the score) read differently, that slang rejects (decided 2026-10-31: "a good reason to reject"), or that Yosys cannot read, cannot be admitted. |
| `P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES` | No construct whose meaning is a synthesis-tool directive: pragmas, attributes, `ifdef SYNTHESIS / YOSYS, translate_off comments. |
| `P-NO-TIME` | No delays, timing, wall-clock or time-dependent behaviour in a combinational task: synthesis ignores them, so the proved (timed) behaviour and the scored netlist would differ. |
| `P-SYNTHESIZABLE` | Not synthesizable hardware, for a design task whose scored artifact is a gate netlist from Yosys `read_verilog -sv`: class declarations, dynamic memory (queues, dynamic and associative arrays), `string` variables and parameters, `real` variables, fork/join, program blocks. The frontend does not read them (measured by `harness/sv/tools_split_audit/yosys_frontend.py`; a constant `real` in a parameter expression IS read), so they are out of scope for now; revisit if a different synthesis frontend is adopted (decided 2026-10-31, about classes: a future synthesis frontend may change that). Host access (file I/O, system calls, DPI) is refused by its own policy, not by this principle. |
| `P-NO-SILENT-PICK` | The PIPELINE tools split (slang / ls-sv for the proof, Yosys for the score, Verilator and Xcelium as simulators give different values for the same text) and no consistent reading exists: refuse loudly, never decide for one side. A split in which only Icarus differs is not a refusal but a declared departure (decided 2026-10-31), and neither is one in which only Xcelium differs from LRM text that slang, Verilator and Yosys follow (decided 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f`). |
| `P-DETERMINISM` | A combinational result must be a function of the inputs, whatever the schedule: randomness is refused, and so is a design with no completed run (it never satisfies `Terminates2`). Where the LRM itself leaves the schedule open (IEEE 4.7) the ruling of 2026-10-31 is that the construct is to be modelled and the golfer proves the output the same in every legal run, not that it is refused for that reason. A simulator-versus-synthesizer mismatch (self-reading `always_comb`: the LRM's answer is deterministic, the synthesizers compute another) is not that case. |
| `P-TRUSTED-BASE` | (added by the register authors, to confirm) The evidence a verdict rests on (checker, trusted statement, generated Goal, axiom set, toolchain) must not be changeable by the submission; a proof is accepted by the kernel from the allowed axioms alone. |
| `P-NO-HOST-ACCESS` | (decided 2026-10-31 for the READING of files; confirmed 2026-11-01 for the rest of the family: "Yes, don't allow this. It's not safe.") The SystemVerilog text of a submission cannot read or write host files, run programs, read the environment or call native code: the checker runs untrusted text on the maintainers' machine (Yosys's read_verilog itself opens the file of a $readmemh). The Lean file of a submission is not scanned for it: it is CONTAINED, by the checker's sandbox around every process that runs submitted text (since 2026-10-31). |

## The pipeline: where a refusal can happen

`check.py` runs the stages in this order and stops at the first that refuses; the stage name is what `tests/expected.json` records.

| stage | what it does | refuses |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | reads `task.json` | unknown keys, a status other than ready / draft, a `ready` task without a reference proof |
| `imports` | checks the Lean file's imports against an allowlist | any import outside Init, Std, Lean, LeanModels.Sv.*, SvGolf.*, tasks.*, Submission.Design and the Mathlib packages (Mathlib, Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient), read from the header as Lean reads it (a comment between two imports separates them) and checked again against the imports Lean recorded in the compiled solution; a second file; `module` / `prelude` headers; a module no package has a source for (a stale name) is a rejection, a package or module missing from the machine (not built, not on the search path, a checkout not at the pinned revision) is an infrastructure error |
| `latency` | reads the latency the solution declares (transaction and stream tasks: `-- svgolf-latency: <n>`, a line of its own) | no such line or more than one, a latency that is not a decimal number from 1 to 999999999, such a line in a task of another kind; later, at the clocked post-synthesis check, a point where the kernel gives no number for the latency or one beyond the checker's limit |
| `source` | `score/srcgate.py`: makes the proved program and the scored program ONE text and strips every comment | preprocessor directives, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments, `unique` / `unique0` / `priority`, x/z/? literal digits, odd characters, host access (file, process, environment, dump and DPI constructs), every procedural `for` header but one narrow shape; in a CLOCKED task also every edge process but `always_ff @(posedge <clock>)` (an asynchronous reset, a second clock, `negedge`, `iff`), a blocking write in it, `initial`, `final`, `always_latch`, a delay or another event control, a declaration initializer |
| `extract` | the pinned Proglib extractor reads the canonical text | whatever the extractor refuses (the language tier), a wrong top module, a parameter list that differs from the task's |
| `banlist` | `score/banlist.py`: pyslang front check plus a Yosys backstop | the run-time operators the task bans, and the run-time `/ % **` that every task bans (since 2026-11-06: a zero divisor makes an x from known inputs), in every disguise Yosys turns into the same cell; also every error of slang's analysis pass (as `fourstate`) |
| `fourstate` | `score/fourstate.py` at every point the checker probes: the scoring point, then the task's probe and backstop points (since 2026-11-06; before, at the scoring point only) | any way an x or z value can arise: constants with unknown bits, out-of-range selects, undriven or conflicting nets, logic loops, latches, and every error of slang's analysis pass (two writers of one variable, mixed continuous and procedural assignment, writing an input port, an `always` without timing control) |
| `clocked_rules` | (clocked tasks) `check/clocked_rules.py`: Python twins of the clocked statements' rules on the envelope at every probe point, before any proof | the constructs rule 3 (`XSafe`, no construct creates an x from known operands) certainly refuses: a run-time `/` or `%` by a divisor that reads a signal, `**` with a signed exponent over a base that reads one, a run-time index that mentions a signal declared signed, a run-time bit select whose index can leave the vector, a run-time indexed part-select read, an x/z literal outside a casez/casex item; a register every write of which is its own value only WARNS here (the `score` stage decides) |
| `trusted` | builds the trusted svGolf modules and the ls-sv evaluator (not timed) | infrastructure only |
| `design` | compiles the generated `Submission.Design` with `load_design_sv2` | loader refusals: cross-checks against slang, the one-driver rule, self-reading `always_comb`, select guards, the multi-point probe check |
| `solution` | compiles `Solution.lean` under the task's time limit: CPU seconds of the Lean process, with a wall-clock backstop of 5 times it | a proof that does not compile in time |
| `integrity` | snapshots the trusted files before and after the solution builds | a solution whose build changes a staged or trusted file (a tripwire, not a sandbox) |
| `comparator` | `check/Comparator.lean`: the kernel accepts `theorem _ : Submission.Goal := Submission.solution` | a missing theorem, a proof of another statement, axioms outside the task's set, `extern` / `implemented_by` |
| `leanchecker` | kernel replay of the submission's modules | declarations added with the kernel check switched off |
| `score` | `score/score.py`: the two-stage Yosys + ABC flow and the GE table | a netlist with cells the table does not price (latches, flip-flops), a non-deterministic flow, a design over the depth budget; in a CLOCKED task (the clocked flow, `score/svgolf_seq.ys`, which runs no fsm pass) a flip-flop the flow removes while reads of it remain and an array lane no write loads (never-loaded), and, as a backstop, a state register the fsm pass re-implements |
| `postsynth` | `check/postsynth.py`: ls-sv and the scored netlist (Verilator) must agree on every vector of the budget | any disagreement, x/z in ls-sv outputs, a netlist Verilator will not build; a rejection is a bug report |
| `ppa` | `score/ppa.py` on the verified netlist: the sky130 area and delay, the ranked numbers | a netlist whose repaired sky130 version is electrically illegal (a load over max_capacitance, a transition over max_transition, a timing-table read outside its characterized range), naming the worst cells |

## Policies

- **Combinational and clocked tasks.** A combinational task's design has no clocked process, no latch and no combinational loop. A clocked task (the transaction, stream and reactive kinds: matmul, sorter, arbiter) admits one clock edge, `always_ff @(posedge <clock>)` with nonblocking writes and a synchronous reset, and no x-creating construct (the group 'Clocked tasks' below).
- **Where the pipeline tools split, the design is refused**, never decided for one side: slang / ls-sv (the proof), Yosys (the score), Verilator and Xcelium are compared, and a shape they read differently is a loud refusal. A difference that only Icarus shows is a declared departure, not a refusal (decided 2026-10-31), and so is one that only Xcelium shows against LRM text the other tools follow (decided 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f` are admitted).
- **A program slang rejects is rejected, and LRM-legal nondeterminism is to be modelled rather than forbidden** (decided 2026-10-31). No construct is admitted on the second ruling yet: the model does not exist, and the audit found that the rows it was first thought to cover are not LRM nondeterminism (self-reading `always_comb`: the LRM's answer is deterministic and the synthesizers compute another; settling combinational loops: refused by fourstate, and some hold state).
- **Everything known that the proof and the score could read differently is refused statically, before any proof is tried** (the source gate at every parameter value; the banlist's run-time `/ % **` in every task; the 4-state rules at the points the checker probes, which narrows and does not close the gap to a statement over every value: svGolf's README.md, "Checker v0 limits"), and the post-synthesis check is the backstop for the disagreements nobody has found.
- **No other restrictions.** Beyond the per-task operator banlist and these safety gates, write any SystemVerilog ls-sv can load.
- **Contestants may add features to ls-sv by pull request, and the maintainers approve every such PR.** See 'How a refusal becomes allowed'.
- **Proofs are symbolic and parametric** (for all N). `bv_decide` is not supported for now (it runs an external SAT solver, which the checker does not support: decided 2026-11-01); `native_decide` is banned in submissions.
- **No host access in the SystemVerilog text.** A submitted design cannot read host files (decided 2026-10-31); by the same principle (confirmed 2026-11-01) it cannot write them, run programs, read the environment, write dumps or call native code. The source gate refuses the constructs; the console tasks (`$display`, `$write`, `$finish`, ...) stay. The Lean file is not scanned for it; the checker's sandbox contains it (see the limits).

## Stage `source`: one program for both tools

Yosys and slang (the frontend your proof is about) read the same file differently when it contains directives, attributes or pragma comments. The gate refuses those and hands every later stage one canonical text with all comments stripped. It also refuses every construct that reaches the machine the checker runs on (`$readmemh`, `$fopen`, `$system`, `$value$plusargs`, `$dumpfile`, DPI, ...): Yosys opens a `$readmemh` file itself while it reads the design.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **conditional compilation on a tool macro**<br>e.g. `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS / `ifdef YOSYS / `ifndef ... `else ... `endif `` | Yosys predefines SYNTHESIS and YOSYS, slang does not: the proof reads one branch, the score the other (a constant, 0 GE). | **never**†: P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES |
| **user macros: `` `define ``, `` `undef ``, a use of a defined macro, `` `__FILE__ ``**<br>e.g. `` `define W 4 `` with a use of `` `W ``; `` `undef FOO ``; a conditional on a user macro | The gate hands the canonical text UNEXPANDED to slang, the extractor and Yosys, so it cannot show that three preprocessors expand a user macro identically. | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: the gate expands user macros itself and hands ONE preprocessed text to every consumer (SYNTHESIS / YOSYS conditions stay refused) [MACROS] |
| **`` `include ``**<br>e.g. `` `include "foo.vh" `` | The included file is a second source the gate, the staging directory, the hash record and the proof never see; include paths differ per tool. | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: multi-file designs with every included file gated, staged and hashed [MULTIFILE] |
| **`` `pragma ``**<br>e.g. `` `pragma protect begin `` | A `` `pragma `` is a tool directive by definition: each tool acts on the pragma names it knows. | **never**†: P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES |
| **other directives: `` `line ``, `` `celldefine ``, `` `resetall ``, `` `begin_keywords ``; `` `default_nettype `` other than none \| wire; a malformed `` `timescale ``**<br>e.g. `` `line 10 "x.sv" 0 ``; `` `default_nettype uwire ``; `` `timescale 1ns `` | Only `` `timescale `` and `` `default_nettype none\|wire `` are on the whitelist: each other directive changes how one tool lexes or elaborates, with no counterpart the gate can show the other tool shares. | **refused-now** |
| **attributes `(* ... *)` and `{* ... *}`**<br>e.g. (* keep *) wire t = a & b; (* full_case *) before a case; even an empty (* *); {* keep *} before a module | Yosys gives attributes (full_case, parallel_case, keep, nosync, keep_hierarchy, blackbox, ...) a synthesis meaning; slang and IEEE simulation give them none. `always @(*)` still passes the gate. | **never**†: P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES |
| **synthesis-pragma comments**<br>e.g. // synopsys translate_off; /* synthesis keep */; // pragma foo; and the words translate_off, translate_on, full_case, parallel_case anywhere in ANY comment | Yosys's lexer reads these comments as directives; slang ignores comments. Refusing is a courtesy; STRIPPING every comment is the guarantee. A comment that merely names full_case is refused too (over-refusal). | **never**†: P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES |
| **`unique`, `unique0`, `priority`**<br>e.g. unique case (a[0]) ... endcase; unique if (...) ... else ...; unique0 case ...; priority case ... | Yosys turns unique into full_case + parallel_case, unique0 into parallel_case, priority into full_case (synthesis don't-cares); ls-sv runs the first matching arm. A unique case that never matches scores 0 GE. | **later**: ls-sv turns a violated qualifier claim into a run-time error on the settled state, so that the termination conjunct forces the proof obligation; the gate refusal goes then [WP5] |
| **a procedural `for` loop header other than the one admitted shape**<br>e.g. `integer i; for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` (the iterator declared outside the header); `for (bit [2:0] i = 0; ...)`; `for (int i = 0; i < 2'd2; i++)`; an iterator spelled like a parameter or another module-scope name | A stopgap (2026-11-04) for three measured mis-models of procedural `for` loops in ls-sv: the condition compared as signed where SystemVerilog compares unsigned, the iterator bound by name (so that it can capture a localparam of the same name), and the iterator's declared type ignored. The gate admits one header shape, in every process: one `int` or `integer` iterator declared in the header with an initial value and a name no module-scope name has, the condition `i <op> E` over unsized decimal literals and the module's own `int` parameters, and one step (`i++`, `i--`, `i += n`, `i -= n`). A generate `for` is not procedural and is not affected. | **later**: ls-sv's fixes of the three mis-models (an unsigned comparison where the operands are unsigned, the iterator in its own scope, the iterator's declared type) |
| **non-ASCII or control characters outside comments; a file that is not UTF-8**<br>e.g. string s = "héllo"; a form feed; a stray 0xFF byte | Identifier and string lexing of non-ASCII text is each tool's business; the gate refuses rather than assume the tools agree (non-ASCII INSIDE a comment passes). | **refused-now** |
| **an unterminated block comment; `//` or `/*` inside a string or an escaped identifier; text slang skips (a syntax error)**<br>e.g. /* never closed; string s = "// not a comment"; assign y = a & b @@ ; | No comment boundary exists, or Yosys's lexer might see a comment that slang does not; skipped or disabled text may still be parsed by Yosys. | **refused-now** |
| **memory-file tasks `$readmemh`, `$readmemb`, `$writememh`, `$writememb`**<br>e.g. initial $readmemh("/etc/hosts", mem); / $readmemb / $writememh / $writememb | Yosys's read_verilog opens the file of a $readmemh/$readmemb itself while it reads the design (Yosys 0.53, measured: the contents become the memory's initial value; one text scores 9.331 GE with one host file and 0 GE with another; a missing file is an error). The pinned flow reads with plain `read_verilog -sv` (no `-defer`), and then Yosys opens the file in a module the top never instantiates as well, but not in a function nobody calls or in a generate branch that is not taken; the gate refuses all of them, because it reads the text. On the machine the checker runs on, that pulls a host file (a salt, an oracle) into the netlist and leaks bits of it through the score; the proof never sees the file. Yosys 0.53 rejects $writememh/$writememb ("Can't resolve task name"), but the gate refuses them first and with a file:line:col. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **file I/O system tasks `$fopen`, `$fclose`, `$fdisplay*`, `$fwrite*`, `$fstrobe*`, `$fmonitor*`, `$fscanf`, `$fgets`, `$fgetc`, `$fread`, `$fseek`, `$ftell`, `$feof`, `$fflush`, `$rewind`, `$ungetc`, `$ferror`**<br>e.g. integer fd; initial begin fd = $fopen("/tmp/x", "w"); $fdisplay(fd, "hi"); $fclose(fd); end / $fscanf(fd, ...) / $fgets / $fread | Opens, reads, writes or repositions a host file (LRM 21.3). Yosys 0.53 has none of these tasks ("Can't resolve function name `\$fopen'"), so without the gate they are rejected late, at the `banlist` stage (at `fourstate` for a task with no banned operators), as an ordinary rejection with Yosys's message and its line in the canonical text but no column and no reason; the gate refuses them at the `source` stage with a file:line:col and the principle, and would still refuse them under a Yosys that accepts them. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **process and environment access `$system`, `$test$plusargs`, `$value$plusargs`, `$getenv`**<br>e.g. initial $system("id"); / initial if ($value$plusargs("X=%d", v)) ... / $test$plusargs("X") / $getenv("HOME") | Runs a host program or reads the host process's environment or command line (LRM 21.6; $system and $getenv are tool extensions). The checker would execute or read them on the machine it runs on. Yosys 0.53 rejects all of them ("Can't resolve task name"); the gate refuses them first. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **wave and dump writers `$dumpfile`, `$dumpvars`, `$dumpon`, `$dumpoff`, `$dumpall`, `$dumplimit`, `$dumpflush`, `$dumpports*`, `$fsdb*`, `$shm_*`, `$vcdplus*`, `$wlf*`**<br>e.g. always_comb begin $dumpfile("/tmp/x.vcd"); $dumpvars(0, band); y = a & b; end / initial begin $dumpfile("/tmp/x.vcd"); $dumpvars(0, band); end | Writes a waveform file on the host (LRM 21.7 and vendor extensions). The one family the pinned Yosys 0.53 ACCEPTS and ignores ($dumpfile, $dumpvars, $dumpon, $dumpoff, $dumpall: a warning only; a design with $dumpfile/$dumpvars scored 5.332 GE like the plain one, measured). Before the gate the form in an `initial` block stopped at the `design` stage (ls-sv has no `initial`, "unknown process kind Initial"; the fixture with the whole family stopped even earlier, at `banlist`, because Yosys rejects $dumpports and $fsdb*), but the form in an `always_comb` block passed every stage up to the proof (score 21.328 GE at N = 16, the same as the plain a & b): the ls-sv extractor lowers a `$dumpfile(...)` / `$dumpvars(...)` statement there to an empty statement, so ls-sv does NOT refuse these two outside `initial`, and the post-synthesis check cannot see them (it simulates the netlist). The other names of the family are errors in Yosys 0.53. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **DPI `import "DPI-C"`, `export "DPI-C"`**<br>e.g. import "DPI-C" pure function int c_fn(input int x); / export "DPI-C" function f; | Native code (LRM 35): an imported function runs whatever the host library does, and an export lets native code call back in. Neither slang's meaning nor Yosys's (a syntax error in Yosys 0.53) is the call's; refused at the gate in the compilation unit and in a module alike. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **`$sdf_annotate`, `$coverage_save`, `$coverage_merge`, `$set_coverage_db_name`, `$load_coverage_db`, and the Annex D file tasks `$input`, `$log`, `$nolog`, `$key`, `$nokey`, `$save`, `$restart`, `$incsave`**<br>e.g. initial begin $sdf_annotate("/tmp/x.sdf"); $coverage_save(0, "/tmp/cov"); $input("/tmp/cmds"); $log("/tmp/out.log"); $save("/tmp/ckpt"); end | Each reads or writes a host file (an SDF file, a coverage database, a command, log, key or checkpoint file; LRM Annex D and the coverage clause). Yosys 0.53 rejects all of them; the gate refuses them first. | **never**: P-NO-HOST-ACCESS |
| **escaped identifier that begins with `$` (`\$readmemh `, `\$clog2 `)**<br>e.g. initial \$readmemh ("/etc/hosts", mem); / function automatic integer \$clog2 (input integer v); ... localparam integer W = \$clog2 (16); | Yosys's lexer gives the escaped identifier the very name of the system task of that spelling (measured: it runs $readmemh and reads the file), while slang reads an ordinary identifier. So even an ADMITTED system name can mean two things: a user function \$clog2 returning 0 is the user's for slang (W = 0, y = 0) and the builtin for Yosys (W = 4, scored as a & b, 5.332 GE). Refused whatever the name. | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| **internal: the canonical text differs from the submitted token stream**<br>e.g. not triggerable by a design (a stripper bug) | Fail closed: the gate validates its own stripping with slang. | **refused-now** (unverified) |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
`timescale 1ns/1ps
module band #(parameter int N = 4)(input logic [N-1:0] a, b, output logic [N-1:0] y);
  // comments are fine: they are stripped
  assign y = a & b;
endmodule
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
`ifdef SYNTHESIS
  assign y = a & b;     // Yosys defines SYNTHESIS, slang does not
`else
  assign y = a | b;
`endif
(* keep *) wire t;      // attribute: Yosys gives it a meaning
// synopsys translate_off
initial $readmemh("/etc/hosts", mem);   // host file: refused
initial $system("id");                 // host program: refused
import "DPI-C" function int c_fn(int x);   // native code: refused
```

## Stage `source` and `fourstate`: no x or z may arise

ls-sv computes with unknown values like an IEEE simulator; Yosys treats them as don't-cares. Wherever an x reaches a decision the proved and the scored circuits can differ, and you choose where. Every SOURCE of an x or z is refused, exactly. A `casez` item may use `z` and `?`, a `casex` item `x`, `z`, `?`.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **x, z or ? digits in a literal outside a casez/casex item wildcard**<br>e.g. 1'bz; 4'b10x0; 'x; 'z; 4'b1??0; 8'hz? in an assign, an == operand, a plain case item, a localparam, a `case inside` item | ls-sv computes with x/z like IEEE simulation (a z item never matches a known input); Yosys reads an x/z bit as a don't-care and drops it from comparisons: complementary items 2'b0z, 2'b1z match no input in ls-sv and EVERY input in Yosys. | **later**: the x-taint feature: allow x sources but forbid x-tainted values from reaching non-monotone decisions; first measure the area gain of don't-cares on a real task [XTAINT] |
| **an x digit in a casez item**<br>e.g. casez (a[1:0]) 2'bx1: ... | Only z and ? are casez wildcards; an x bit in a casez item is NOT a wildcard and the two tools read it differently. | **later**: as for x/z literals (x-taint feature) [XTAINT] |
| **a constant with unknown bits: parameter, localparam, inline constant, constant function result, out-of-range constant select**<br>e.g. localparam logic [3:0] K = 4'd1 / 4'd0; a constant function returning an unassigned local; v[6 +: 4] on [7:0]; an enum member with an x value | Constant division by zero is not banned as arithmetic but it is x: ls-sv computes with it, Yosys reads it as a don't-care. | **later**: the x-taint feature [XTAINT] |
| **a run-time index whose type can address outside the declared range**<br>e.g. logic [N-1:0] mem [3:0]; y = mem[i] with a 3-bit i (0..7 on [3:0]); a signed index; v[i +: 4] with a 3-bit i on [7:0] | An out-of-range read is x. The rule reasons from the index TYPE alone (an unsigned w-bit index ranges 0..2^w-1): exact for the checker's purpose but it over-refuses indexes the design keeps in range by other means. Fix: declare a power-of-two range or narrow the index. | **later**: the x-taint feature (and value-range reasoning on the index expression to narrow the over-refusal, a proposal) [XTAINT] |
| **a procedural loop counter used as an index**<br>e.g. always_comb begin for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) y[k] = a[k] & b[k]; end | The run-time index rule reasons from index TYPES and does not know loop bounds, so it refuses an `int` loop counter used as an index (ls-sv loads such a loop: the extractor expands it since 2026-11-01, and the source gate admits one header shape). The generate-for twin passes. | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: rule (d) learns loop bounds [LOOPS] |
| **a select with no fixed range or a non-constant width**<br>e.g. (not triggered: a queue reports a fixed range; slang rejects a non-constant width) | Cannot show the index stays in range. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a net that is used but has no driver**<br>e.g. logic u; t = u ? 0 : 1; an unassigned output | ls-sv reads the net as x; Yosys resolves it freely (to whatever makes the logic smallest): the proved and the scored circuits differ at a point the player chooses. | **later**: the x-taint feature [XTAINT] |
| **conflicting drivers on one net, a combinational logic loop**<br>e.g. two continuous assigns to one net; assign t = a & u; assign u = t \| a; | Bus contention is not a combinational function; a loop is not a combinational function either (and the statement refuses every loop itself since 2026-11-06: LoopFree). | **never**†: P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| **an inferred latch**<br>e.g. always_comb begin if (en) y = a; end (an output not assigned on every path) | A variable an always_comb block reads before it assigns it on every path holds x; Yosys `proc` refuses it ('Latch inferred ... from always_comb'). Since 2026-11-06 the banlist backstop runs for every task (every task bans run-time / % **), so a latch an always_comb block infers meets Yosys's own `proc` refusal there first (aes_sbox/case_missing_nodefault stops at `banlist`); this rule refuses the latches `proc` infers without an error (always @*, always_latch). | **later**: latch semantics in ls-sv, a statement that admits a latch (the combinational statement refuses every latch: `LoopFree`) and a latch price in score/ge.json [SEQ] |
| **a design Yosys 0.53 cannot read at the scoring point, or any slang error there**<br>e.g. a syntax error; a function with `return`; a queue declaration; GenvarUnknownBits | Fail closed: a design Yosys cannot read cannot be scored. Yosys 0.53 is narrower than slang. | **refused-now** |
| **an error of slang's analysis pass (two writers of one variable, mixed assignments, a written input, an `always` without timing control)**<br>e.g. always_comb cout = c[N]; always_comb cout = c[N]; / assign cout = c[N]; always_comb cout = c[N]; / assign cin = a[0]; / initial cout = 0; always_comb cout = c[N]; / always cout = c[N]; | A program slang's driver rejects is rejected (decided 2026-11-01, analysis errors included). Yosys accepts several of them silently and the Lean loader refused them only by accident or not at all (`initial` plus `always_comb`: the loader has no `Initial` process kind). | **never**: P-SAME-PROGRAM |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
always_comb begin
  casez (a[1:0])
    2'b1?: y = 1'b1;     // wildcard digit in a casez item: allowed
    default: y = 1'b0;
  endcase
end
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
assign y = a[0] ? 1'bz : a[1];     // z literal
localparam logic [1:0] K = 2'd1 / 2'd0;   // constant division by zero is x
logic [3:0] m; ... m[{1'b1, a[1:0]}]     // index can leave the range: x
logic u; assign y = u ? a : b;           // u is undriven
```

## Stage `banlist`: the task's banned operators

A task bans the run-time operator that IS the task, plus whatever Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc turns `+` and `-` chains into the cells of `*`). Constant arithmetic (parameters, genvar loops, index arithmetic over parameters and genvars) and equality stay allowed. A task that bans `+` or `-` also bans run-time ordering comparisons (`< <= > >=`; decided 2026-11-05), which Yosys builds as its own adder. Which operators are banned is per task: `add`, `mul` and `_example` ban `+ - * / % **`; `clmul` bans `+ - *`; `fdivp` bans `/ % **` (and keeps every comparison); every task bans run-time `/ % **`.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **a run-time `+ - * / % **` in a task that bans it**<br>e.g. assign y = a + b; a - b; a * b; a / b; a % b; a ** b; with run-time operands | The operator that IS the task, plus what Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc: + and - chains become the cells of *). Constant arithmetic stays allowed. Which operators: tasks/*/task.json banlist.operators. | **refused-now** |
| **a run-time `/ % **` in ANY task, whatever its own banlist**<br>e.g. assign q = 1'b1 / ~rare; a % b; a ** e; with run-time operands, in clmul, aes_sbox, matmul or sorter as in the tasks that ban them anyway | A zero divisor (or 0 ** a negative exponent) makes an x from KNOWN operands (IEEE 1800 11.4.2). ls-sv carries it into a decision (`if (x)` takes the else branch) while Yosys builds a defined value, and with a 2-state destination IEEE itself defines the value (0) and Yosys builds another, so the scored circuit can differ from the proved one on the one input that divides by zero (2^-32 of the inputs in clmul/div_zero_x, which the post-synthesis vectors miss). No 4-state rule can be exact about it, so the operators are banned: banlist.py ALWAYS_BANNED, added to every task's list by task_banlist, front check and backstop, with the rule in the message. Constants and parameter, genvar and localparam arithmetic stay allowed. | **refused-now** |
| **a run-time ordering comparison `< <= > >=` in a task that bans `+` or `-`**<br>e.g. assign c = a > ~b; a[0] < b[0]; x <= 5; with run-time operands | Yosys's alumacc builds a run-time ordering comparison as an $alu, Yosys's own adder (a > ~b IS the carry out of a + b, so an adder whose every carry is a comparison is Yosys's adder), so after proc; opt the backstop also runs alumacc and rejects every $alu / $macc / $lcu / $fa cell it builds, at the comparison's source location. Equality (== != === !==), comparisons over parameters and genvars (folded as constants) and a comparator built from & \| ^ ~ stay allowed; a task that bans neither + nor - keeps every comparison. | **refused-now** |
| **the same arithmetic in other forms: compound assignment, unary minus, ++ / --, array .sum() / .product(), $countones & co, run-time index arithmetic**<br>e.g. y += a; -a; x++; arr.sum(); $countones(a); a[j + 1]; x[sel*W +: W] | Each builds the same $add / $sub / $mul / $neg cell. Procedural for-loop counters (k++) and constant arguments stay allowed. Yosys 0.53 cannot read .sum() at all, a later one may. | **refused-now** |
| **a banned operator hidden behind a constant-argument function call, in a generate branch the scoring point does not take, or behind a loop counter that is written**<br>e.g. function automatic logic [15:0] g(input int k); g = a / 16; endfunction assign q = g(0); for (int k...) begin k = int'(a[0]); ... end | A call is constant only when its arguments are AND its body reads nothing but its own arguments and locals; Yosys silently ignores a write to a loop counter and folds the loop, simulation does not (the proof and the score then differ). | **refused-now** |
| **a design Yosys or slang cannot read at a backstop point**<br>e.g. syntax Yosys 0.53 lacks (arr.sum()); an undeclared identifier | A design Yosys cannot read cannot be scored; the front check cannot walk what slang rejects. The banlist fails closed. | **refused-now** |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
for (genvar i = 0; i < N; i++) begin : g
  assign s[i] = a[i] ^ b[i] ^ c[i];     // gates, not +
  assign c[i+1] = (a[i] & b[i]) | (c[i] & (a[i] ^ b[i]));   // i+1 is constant arithmetic
end
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
assign s = a + b + cin;          // run-time + in a task that bans it
assign y = a * b;                // run-time *
assign n = $countones(a);        // Yosys builds it from $add cells
assign p = arr.sum();            // array reduction = run-time +
```

## Stages `extract` and `design`: the language tier and the parameter list

The proof is about what the pinned extractor and the ls-sv loader accept. A construct they refuse fails here with the tier's own message. The top module's overridable parameters must be exactly the task's, by name and order, because the scoring script overrides them by name.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **the extractor refused the design**<br>e.g. anything the pinned extractor refuses: a missing top module, a parameter the probe points name that the top lacks, any Unsupported construct | The proof can only be about what the extractor reads. A pass-through for the language tier's refusals (docs/sv-refusals.md). | **refused-now** |
| **an envelope that loads but contains an Unsupported process or expression**<br>e.g. a cast to a parameter width (`N'(x)`), `$signed(x)` in a wider context, a gate primitive (`and g(y, a, b)`), a function local read before it is assigned, any construct the extractor embeds as an `Unsupported` node instead of refusing | The extractor exits 0 and `load_design_sv2` builds `design.sem` even when a construct is unsupported: the node is kept as a loud `Process2.unsupported`/`Unsupported` expression and refuses only when run. No proof about such a design can hold, so the `design` stage rejects it before any proof, scoring or leaderboard step, naming the first loud node, at the scoring point and at every probe point not larger than it. | **refused-now** |
| **the top's overridable parameters differ from the task's**<br>e.g. an extra `parameter int M = 2` (localparams are free) | The scoring script overrides the parameter by name (-chparam N 16); another name or an extra parameter would score a different circuit than the one proved. | **refused-now** |
| **the design does not load (ls-sv refused it)**<br>e.g. loader refusals: cross-checks, the one-driver rule, AlwaysComb:self-read / alias-read, select guards, the probe cross-check; a parameter declared narrower than int | Pass-through for the loader's refusals; the cross-check at the scoring point keeps the scored design one ls-sv and slang agree on. | **refused-now** (unverified) |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
module band #(parameter int N = 4)(input logic [N-1:0] a, b, output logic [N-1:0] y);
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
module band #(parameter int N = 4, parameter int M = 2)(...);   // an extra parameter
module band #(parameter bit [3:0] N = 4)(...);               // narrower than int: N = 16 reads as 0
```

## Stage `imports`: the proof file

The checker builds only SvGolf, the task modules and the evaluator; a module outside the allowlist is unaudited code outside the trusted base. Mathlib and its packages (Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient) are on the allowlist. One solution file in v0.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **imports outside the allowlist**<br>e.g. import LeanModels.Python.Semantics; import Examples.python.tri.proof; import Mathlib2.Tactic; import Lake | The checker builds only SvGolf, tasks and svgolf-eval, so a module outside the allowlist is code nobody audited and stays outside the trusted base. Mathlib and the packages its import closure reaches (Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient: the module roots, pinned by Proglib's lake-manifest.json) ARE admitted since 2026-10-31: a proof that uses them is accepted on the same terms as any other, by the kernel from the task's allowed axioms alone. The comparator walks the dependency closure for axioms (a `native_decide` behind a Mathlib lemma is rejected like one in the file) and REPLAYS that closure, minus the toolchain and the submission's own modules, through the kernel, so a package olean whose declaration was added without kernel checking is rejected; toolchain modules must resolve into the toolchain; the integrity tripwire watches the Lean search path (`.olean` files of the packages, entries that do not exist) for every solution; the imports Lean recorded in the compiled solution are compared with the header the checker read. | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE |
| **a second solution file**<br>e.g. import MyHelpers | One file in v0: there is no module the checker could stage or hash for a second file. | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: multi-file staging, hashing and an integrity snapshot of every player file [MULTIFILE] |
| **the solution must `import Submission.Design`**<br>e.g. a Solution.lean without that import | The theorem must be about the design the checker extracted. | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| **`module` or `prelude` headers; a dangling `import`**<br>e.g. a Lean file starting with `module` or `prelude` | The header parser (comment stripper plus token scan) only understands ordinary import headers. | **refused-now** |
| **(transaction and stream tasks) a solution without exactly one latency line, or a latency line in a task of another kind**<br>e.g. two `-- svgolf-latency:` lines; `-- svgolf-latency: 0`; a latency line in a combinational task | The goal pins the latency at the scoring point (`lat p₀ = n`) and the score uses n, so a transaction or stream solution declares it in exactly one header line `-- svgolf-latency: <n>`, a decimal number of cycles from 1 to 999999999; at the clocked post-synthesis check the kernel's value at each point must be a number within the checker's limit. | **refused-now** |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
import Submission.Design
import LeanModels.Sv.Ingest2
import SvGolf.Comb
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
import Examples.python.tri.proof
import LeanModels.Python.Semantics
import Mathlib2.Tactic     -- a lookalike
import MyHelpers
```

## The trusted statement: interface, clocks, termination, function, range

The statement is a Lean `Prop` fixed by the task: `SvGolf/Task.lean` for the combinational tasks, `SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean` and `SvGolf/TaskReact.lean` for the clocked ones. A combinational design that satisfies it has exactly the task's ports, no clocked process and no combinational loop, a completed run for every schedule and stimulus, and the task's function at every cycle, for every parameter value in the range; a clocked design meets the task's guarantee in every run from every power-up state, at every parameter value in the range. These are not rules you can argue with: a design that breaks one has no proof of the statement, and the repository checks the refutations in `tests/*/negative/Refute.lean`.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **ports that are not EXACTLY the task's (names, order, widths)**<br>e.g. an extra or hidden input (en, a rounding-mode pin); a renamed port (ci for cin); a wider or merged output; an inout; a port one bit wider than the task's (two mutants of the arbiter's reference) | Stimulus conventions ignore unknown names and store values at their own width, so only pinned ports mean what the hypothesis says. Since 2026-11-07 (decided after a mutation test of the arbiter) the `extract` stage also compares the extractor's ports at every probe point (the defaults when a task has none) with task.json `ports` (the input ports in declaration order with their widths, then the outputs likewise, no other direction), for every kind, before any proof: the statement's `Interface` at those points. Before, a port one bit wider passed every check that needs no proof (`--unproved` called those two mutants admissible) and only the proof, which cannot exist, stood in its way. | **refused-now** |
| **(combinational tasks) any edge-phase process (always_ff, always @(posedge clk), an async-reset block), even with a dead clock**<br>e.g. always_ff @(posedge clk) s <= a ^ b; clock tied low or undriven | A combinational task's statement requires `Unclocked`: ls-sv runs every edge-phase process once per cycle whatever its clock holds, so a register on a clock nothing drives holds the right value in ls-sv and x in every simulator (0 GE in Yosys). Clocked designs are the clocked tasks' (the transaction, stream and reactive kinds), whose statements model the clock edge. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a design that never settles or has no completed run (Terminates2)**<br>e.g. an oscillating combinational loop; a design the loader refused (errorDesign) | Models2 quantifies over completed runs only, so a design that never settles satisfies every property vacuously; Terminates2 requires a completed run for every schedule and stimulus. | **never**†: P-DETERMINISM (unverified) |
| **a combinational loop or a latch, even one that settles (LoopFree)**<br>e.g. always_comb u = t; always_comb if (u) t = 1'b1; else t = 1'b0; always_comb if (en) q = d; one assign that reads a window it writes | A run starts every variable at x and settles, so a loop is read at one state while a circuit powers up in any 0/1 state the loop can hold; the statement does not quantify over those states and requires LoopFree instead: the design lowers (Design2.lowerComb, which refuses a latch) to continuous assigns with an Acyclic rank, the certificate the proof helpers already use. The rank is on processes, not bits, so it also refuses a process-level cycle in which no bit depends on itself (write such bits as separate assigns). | **never**†: P-SYNTHESIZABLE (unverified) |
| **outputs that are not exactly the task's function at EVERY cycle with fully known inputs**<br>e.g. the wrong function; an output left x/z; correct only at the scoring point; outputs depending on earlier cycles | The conjunct holds at every cycle of every run, whatever the earlier stimulus; a design cannot keep the hypothesis false by driving its own inputs. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a clocked transaction that misses the frozen TxTask guarantee: done not within lat cycles of the start edge, or done and the payload not held at result x until the next accepted start or reset**<br>e.g. an off-by-one step counter; unsigned instead of signed products; a missing sign extension; done one cycle early; the accumulator not cleared on start; an accumulator truncated to 2W | `TxTask.StatementV2` (`SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean`) claims `Guar` for every transaction under `Released` and `Rely`, in every run from every power-up state on every known stimulus, at every parameter point in range, and the proof must establish it; a design wrong at any point, or late by a cycle, fails at the solution stage. Each matmul attack that reaches the post-synthesis check is also wrong there (`check.py --unproved`; `async_reset` stops before it, at `source`), so none is merely different. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a clocked stream that misses the frozen StreamTask guarantee: out_valid unknown or raised before the first start, or a transaction's out_valid cycles not emitting exactly spec xs (the input sorted ascending, duplicates kept) within lat cycles of the start edge**<br>e.g. the token shift reading the cell's own token (no value ever emitted); a missing else (two writes, the later wins); the neighbour push comparing the cell's own value; the valid token entering with the start (out_valid one cycle early, one value too many); a reset that leaves the cells; a top cell the drain does not clear; signed instead of unsigned order | `StreamTask.StatementV2` (`SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean`) claims `Guar` for every transaction under `Released` and `Rely`, in every run from every power-up state on every known stimulus, at every parameter point in range, and the proof must establish it; a design wrong at any point, or one value early or late, fails at the solution stage. Each sorter attack but `rst_gate` is also wrong at post-synthesis (`check.py --unproved`), so none is merely different; `rst_gate`'s snapshots are right, and only the proof refuses it (rule 1, `MooreOutDep`); designs that differ from the reference only in how they order EQUAL values (`>=` for `>`) are not attacks, since equal values are interchangeable in the emitted list. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **(transaction and stream tasks) an output in the combinational cone of an input port, the reset included: the clocked statements' rule 1 (`MooreOutDep d []`), with nothing exempt since 2026-11-09**<br>e.g. assign out_valid = ov_q & ~rst (tests/sorter/attacks/rst_gate.sv: every snapshot right, the last output before a reset hidden on the wire); an output that reads start or an operand combinationally | `TxTask.SatisfiedAtV2` and `StreamTask.SatisfiedAtV2` (`SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean`) ask `MooreOutDep d []`: no combinational path, control dependencies included, from any input port to an output port, so that every claimed snapshot is what the outputs show on the wire for the whole next period. Until 2026-11-09 `rst` was exempt, which let a reset-gated output hide the snapshot before a reset entry, a snapshot the claims still cover (found in the statements' review). The post-synthesis check does not look for this (the snapshots are right), so the proof must establish it: such a design fails at the solution stage, and the kernel refutes it for every latency (tests/sorter/negative/Refute.lean, `rst_gate_refuted`). | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a reactive controller that misses the ReactTask guarantee: from some power-up state, a reset snapshot that does not show atReset, an unsafe cycle, an obligation triggered at K + 1 consecutive entries and answered in none of them, or an output in the combinational cone of an input**<br>e.g. the arbiter's attacks: never grant; grant every requester; always client 0; fixed priority; a free-running or a request-gated token ring; the right grant one cycle late; a sticky or a stale-mask round-robin; a rotation that wraps at 2^clog2(N); a Mealy grant; a grant flop with no reset; arbitration every other cycle; fixed priority after 4095 cycles. Its negatives: a never-reset 2-state ring `u` that gives fixed priority when `&u`; a flag set at the first reset edge from the pre-reset `&u` | `ReactTask.Statement` (svgolf/SvGolf/TaskReact.lean; the arbiter's instance, tasks/arbiter/Spec.lean) claims, from every power-up state, under every schedule, on every known stimulus, at every reset release and for every list of inputs, that the reset snapshot shows `atReset` (the arbiter's G0) and every later snapshot meets safety (`Safe`: G1 to G3) and bounded response (`Responds`: G4 with K = N - 1), with the output discipline `MooreOut` (no combinational path from an input port to an output port) and rule 3 (`XSafe`); the proof must establish it at every parameter point in range, so a design wrong at any point fails at the solution stage. Each arbiter attack that reaches the post-synthesis check is also wrong there (`a13_async` stops at `source` and `a16_xopt` at `score`; `check.py --unproved`: the reactive check holds the netlist's outputs to the guarantee on the oracle's segments, a 70000-entry reset-free run among them, and samples the outputs before every edge for the Moore discipline), so none is merely different. The two negatives are right from ls-sv's own start (x, or 0 for a 2-state variable) and wrong from a power-up state the netlist can take (`u` all ones); they pass every stage before the proof and are refuted in the kernel (tests/arbiter/negative/Refute.lean). | **refused-now** |
| **a proof that holds at the scoring point N = 16 only**<br>e.g. a ripple adder at N = 16, carry-free elsewhere | The statement quantifies over every N in the task's range (1 <= N < 2^31 in _example and add, 1 <= N < 2^30 in mul and clmul, so that every width stays an int), so a one-width proof does not typecheck; a fixed-size task (aes_sbox) is StatementFixed. | **refused-now** (unverified) |

What is refused:

```systemverilog
module adder(input logic [N-1:0] a, b, input logic ci, ...);   // port named ci, not cin
output logic [N:0] s;                                           // merged {cout, sum}
always_ff @(posedge clk) s <= a ^ b;                           // any edge process
```

## Stages `comparator`, `leanchecker`, `integrity`: the proof itself

The kernel must accept your theorem from the task's allowed axioms alone. Everything that would let a proof depend on something other than the kernel is refused.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **no theorem `Submission.solution`**<br>e.g. a Solution.lean that defines no such theorem, or defines it with `def` | The comparator asks the kernel to accept `theorem _ : Submission.Goal := Submission.solution`. | **refused-now** |
| **a proof of another statement**<br>e.g. theorem solution : True := trivial | The accepted theorem must be exactly the generated Goal, checked by the kernel against the solution's type and proof term. | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **`sorry` and `admit`**<br>e.g. theorem t : ... := by sorry; also a goal ADMITTED by a tactic after it logged an error (the `sv_structure` tactics log their refusal and admit the goal, so the proof compiles with an error and depends on sorryAx) | The proof depends on sorryAx, which the allow list excludes. | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **`native_decide`**<br>e.g. theorem t : ... := by native_decide | native_decide trusts the compiled evaluator, not the kernel: it adds a per-declaration axiom `<decl>._native.native_decide.ax_1_1` that no static allow list can name. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **`bv_decide` (and `allow_bv_decide: true` in a task)**<br>e.g. theorem t : ... := by bv_decide; task.json allow_bv_decide: true | bv_decide runs an external SAT solver (the toolchain's `cadical`), and the checker does not support external solvers (decided 2026-11-01: "Let's not support external solvers for now"). Supporting it needs the solution's compile sandbox to grant `fork`, the exec of `cadical` and a writable temporary directory (measured: all three), which also lets a hostile file start further copies of `lean`. Without the grant the tactic fails in the sandbox with `operation not permitted` (check.py adds a hint at `solution`); with --sandbox off the comparator rejects the generated axiom `<decl>._native.bv_decide.ax_*`, naming the policy; `allow_bv_decide: true` is an infrastructure error. The comparator's re-verification of the axiom and the sandbox grant are kept, dormant, behind the constant `BV_DECIDE_SUPPORTED` in check.py. | **refused-now** |
| **a hand-declared axiom**<br>e.g. axiom cheat : Goal | Only the task's allowed_axioms may appear in the solution's dependency closure, walked through kernel values (not the #print axioms cache). | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **`extern` / `implemented_by` on submission constants**<br>e.g. @[implemented_by fastId] def slowId | They only matter for compiled code, which native evaluation can reach: the compiled meaning would differ from the kernel meaning the statement is about. | **never**: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **declarations added with the kernel check switched off**<br>e.g. Environment.addDeclCore ... (doCheck := false) for the top theorem or for a helper lemma | A proof must be replayable by the kernel from scratch (the comparator catches the top theorem, leanchecker the helpers). | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **a solution whose build changes a trusted file**<br>e.g. tactics or #eval that change the staging tree, score/*.py, check/*, svgolf-eval, simcells.v, the svGolf / LeanModels.Sv builds, the toolchain, Yosys, Verilator, the C++ compiler | A tripwire, not a sandbox (an escaping process or tamper-and-restore is beyond it). A concurrent rebuild of LeanModels.Sv also trips it. | **never**†: P-TRUSTED-BASE (unverified) |
| **the proof or the replay overruns its time limit**<br>e.g. Solution.lean using more CPU seconds than task.json time_limit_s, or more wall-clock seconds than its backstop (5 times the limit); comparator or leanchecker using more CPU seconds than verify_time_limit_s, or more wall-clock seconds than its backstop (5 times it) | Bounded checking time. The proof limit counts the CPU seconds of the Lean process (decided 2026-11-05), and so do the comparator's and leanchecker's (since 2026-11-06), so the machine's load does not count; the wall-clock backstop stops a proof or a replay that waits instead of computing. None of them counts the wait for the Lean slot wrapper. | **refused-now** (unverified) |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by
  -- induction on bit indices, decide +kernel for fixed-size subgoals
  ...
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by native_decide   -- trusts the compiler
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by sorry
axiom cheat : Submission.Goal
```

## Stages `score` and `postsynth`: the scored netlist

The `score` stage synthesizes the design with the pinned Yosys + ABC flow (area in NAND2 gate equivalents and depth, exploration columns); the `ppa` stage weighs the verified netlist on the sky130 cells, the ranked area and delay. The post-synthesis check then simulates ls-sv and the scored netlist on the task's vector budget and rejects any difference; it is sampling, so a difference confined to a tiny input region can slip through, which is what the static rules above are for. A rejection here is a bug report: either ls-sv or Yosys is wrong.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **(combinational tasks) a netlist with cells the GE table does not price**<br>e.g. always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b; (a $_DFF_P_ survives into the netlist) | A combinational task's netlist contains only AND/NAND/OR/NOR/XOR/XNOR/ANDNOT/ORNOT/MUX/NOT; a latch or a flip-flop is not scored there (the clocked tasks' flow prices flip-flops: score/ge_seq.json). | **refused-now** |
| **Yosys cannot synthesize the design; the gate refused it; non-deterministic synthesis; depth over the task's budget**<br>e.g. a syntax error; score.py without --no-gate on a refused file; --repeat K with differing results | No netlist, no score; a score must be reproducible. The depth budget is live but unexercised (every current task sets depth_budget null). | **refused-now** |
| **ls-sv and the scored netlist differ on a vector**<br>e.g. any vector of the budget on which ls-sv's evaluation of the design (design.sem) and the Verilator netlist model differ | The proof is about ls-sv's reading, the score about Yosys's: the backstop for disagreements nobody has found. It is sampling: a difference confined to a rare region can pass. A rejection is a bug report. | **refused-now** |
| **latent x sources ls-sv does not support yet: a function local read before assignment, a never-loaded always_latch, always @* with a path that assigns nothing**<br>e.g. tests/_example/attacks/fn_uninit.sv (rejected at `design`; the postsynth check alone rejects it too), latch_never.sv and latch_star.sv (rejected at `fourstate` since 2026-11-01; before, at `design`) | x in IEEE, resolved freely by Yosys (to 1 or 0), and no static rule sees it. ls-sv inlines a function that is a pure function of its inputs (since 2026-11-02) but not one that reads a local before assigning it, has no `always_latch`, and runs `always @*` only where it means `always_comb`, so such a design loads with an Unsupported node and the `design` stage rejects it (`Design2.hasUnsupported`); the postsynth stage, alone, still fails closed on it. Since 2026-11-01 the latch half is also closed at the original text: rule (e) of score/fourstate.py refuses any latch `proc` infers (`select -assert-none t:$dlatch t:$adlatch t:$dlatchsr`), whatever ls-sv models, and `fourstate` runs before `design`. | **later**: for a function local read before assignment: a 4-state rule in score/fourstate.py must land before ls-sv models such a function; the latch half is done (fourstate.py rule (e)); a latch construct ls-sv models would still need a rule for its initial x [LATCH4] |
| **fail-closed postsynth conditions: x/z in an ls-sv output, an unknown-valued constant that a gate, a flip-flop or an output reads, a netlist Verilator will not lint / build / run, σ_src ≠ σ_rev, port sets that differ, a netlist that does not re-read, an inout port, a non-plain identifier**<br>e.g. a tied-low clock leaves a 16'hx constant in the netlist and rejects every vector | Verilator is 2-state and would silently turn an unknown constant into 0 or 1; a result that depends on the schedule is not a combinational function; everything unclear fails closed. | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| **a netlist whose repaired sky130 version is electrically illegal**<br>e.g. a load over max_capacitance; a transition over max_transition; a timing-table read outside its characterized range | The ranked score is the sky130 area and delay of the verified netlist after the pinned repair; a netlist the liberty cannot time without extrapolating has no delay to rank, so the `ppa` stage refuses it and names the worst cells. | **refused-now** |

What is refused:

```systemverilog
always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b;    // a flip-flop in the netlist: not priced
```

## Clocked tasks: one clock edge, no x-creating construct, no never-loaded register

A clocked task (the sequential, transaction, stream and reactive kinds) adds refusals of its own. The source gate's clocked rules (`score/srcgate.py`, item 6) admit an edge process only as `always_ff @(posedge <clock>)` with nonblocking writes (and a `for` header's step on its own iterator), and no `initial`, `final`, `always_latch`, delay, `wait`, `fork` or declaration initializer; the edge rule exists because the loader drops what the clocked semantics cannot express (an asynchronous reset, a `negedge` clock, an `iff` guard), and ls-sv would then prove a different, synchronous circuit. The `clocked_rules` stage refuses before the proof the x-creating constructs that rule 3 of the statement forbids (the statement stays the authority). The `score` stage refuses a design where the pinned flow removes a flip-flop while reads of it remain, or connects the reads of an array lane no write loads to an undefined value: Yosys resolves each such read separately, while ls-sv gives a register one power-up value for every read (decided 2026-11-06: svGolf disallows a design where the pinned Yosys deviates from the semantics). The clocked flow runs no fsm pass (`synth -nofsm`, decided 2026-11-06), so a state register keeps its own flip-flops.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **(clocked tasks) an edge process other than `always_ff @(posedge <clock>)`: an asynchronous reset or a second clock in its sensitivity list, a `negedge`, `edge` or level-sensitive event, an `iff` guard on the clock, a clock other than the task's**<br>e.g. always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst) (tests/arbiter/attacks/a13_async.sv, tests/matmul/attacks/async_reset.sv); always_ff @(negedge clk); always_ff @(posedge clk iff en) | The loader drops the extractor's `areset`, `edge: neg` and `iff` fields, so each of these shapes would reach ls-sv as a plain `always_ff @(posedge clk)`, a different circuit from the one Yosys scores (an asynchronous reset changes the outputs inside a period, and the scoring flow has no asynchronous-reset flop), and the statement's `ClockedBy clk none` cannot see a dropped field. So the source gate's clocked rules refuse them in every clocked kind: the reset is synchronous. | **refused-now** |
| **(clocked tasks) what the clock-step profile does not run: `initial`, `final`, `always_latch`, a delay, `wait`, `fork` or another event control, a blocking write in an `always_ff` body (but the step of a `for` header's own iterator), an initializer on a declaration**<br>e.g. `initial q = '0;` `always_ff @(posedge clk) q = d;` `logic [3:0] cnt = '0;` `#1 q <= d;` | The clocked statements update every register from the same pre-edge state, so a blocking write that another process could see is a race, and the profile has no initial values, delays or latches: the power-up state is any state, and the reset is the design's own. The source gate refuses these in every clocked kind before the proof. | **refused-now** |
| **(clocked tasks) an x-creating construct, refused before the proof by the twin of rule 3 (`XSafe`)**<br>e.g. q <= a / b with b a signal; a ** e with a signed exponent e; v[i] with i declared signed; v[i] where i can leave the vector; v[i +: 4] read; 4'b1x00 outside a casez/casex item | Rule 3 of the clocked statements (`XSafe`, `SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean`, decided 2026-11-06) forbids every construct that can create an x from known operands, so that every value of every run from every power-up state is known; the statement is the authority and the proof must establish it. check/clocked_rules.py refuses early, with a message per construct, only what ls-sv's lowering certainly turns into a construct `xsWidth` refuses, and admits the rest to the proof (tests/checker/test_xsafe_twin.py: the twin and `xsafeB` agree on the counter's and the arbiter's fixtures). | **refused-now** |
| **(clocked tasks) a never-loaded register: a flip-flop the pinned flow removes while reads of it remain**<br>e.g. u <= u read by if (!u) (tests/arbiter/attacks/a16_xopt.sv); a register loaded only under a condition that is never true or an enable that is never active; a register whose only load is an undefined value | The pinned Yosys removes a flip-flop whose next value is always its own, whose enable is never active or whose clock is constant (its log: `Handling D = Q ... (removing D path)`), or whose only load is an undefined value (a constant x), and resolves each READ of the undefined value separately, while ls-sv gives a register one power-up value for every read, so the proved and the scored circuits differ (a16_xopt: every snapshot fair in ls-sv, the scored netlist fixed priority). The verdict is the scored run's own log (`score.flop_removals`), at the scoring point and at every post-synthesis point; a register whose every read folds away is removed as unread and accepted, and one loaded with a constant 0 or 1 gives every read one value and is accepted. An undriven net, the combinational analogue, is the `fourstate` stage's. Write: reset it, load it with a value other than its own, or remove it. | **refused-now** |
| **(clocked tasks) a never-loaded memory lane: a bit lane of an unpacked array that no write loads, read**<br>e.g. an array read at a constant index and never written (tests/seq_counter/never_loaded/mem_rom_const.sv); a write that never reaches the lane (mem_dead_write.sv, mem_unreached_word.sv) | opt_mem connects every read of a lane no write loads with a defined value to an undefined value before any flip-flop exists (its log: `removing const-x lane`), which Yosys resolves separately at each read, while ls-sv gives every word one power-up value for every read. MEASURED (2026-11-06): the arbiter reference plus an unwritten two-word array read at a constant index, decided both ways at one cycle count, passed every stage before this rule and withheld the grant at entry 131071 (measured in the review of the clocked statements). A lane every write loads with the constant 0 or 1 gives every read one value and is accepted (`ok_mem_const0.sv`). Write: write the lane, or replace the array by constants. | **refused-now** |
| **(clocked tasks, a backstop) a state register re-implemented by Yosys's fsm pass**<br>e.g. none in the pinned flow, which runs `synth -nofsm`; before 2026-11-06 a state register read only by comparisons with constants was recoded one-hot, with or without a reset (tests/seq_counter/never_loaded/fsm_unreset.sv, fsm_reset.sv) | The fsm pass re-encodes a state register from the state codes it extracts: the new flip-flops power up in codes that are no value of the register, and a value that is no extracted state has no code, while ls-sv gives the register one power-up value of its width, so the proved and the scored circuits differ from some power-ups (found in the review of the clocked statements). Since 2026-11-06 the clocked flow runs `synth -nofsm` (the combinational flow is unchanged), so a state register keeps its own flip-flops and the log has no `Mapping FSM` line; should one appear, the `score` stage refuses the design and asks for a report to the maintainers. | **refused-now** |

What you can write:

```systemverilog
always_ff @(posedge clk)            // one clock, one edge
  if (rst) begin                     // a synchronous reset
    gnt <= '0;
    mask <= '1;
  end else begin
    gnt <= pick;                     // nonblocking writes only
    if (pick != '0) mask <= ~((pick << 1) - 1'b1);
  end
```

What is refused:

```systemverilog
always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst)   // an asynchronous reset: refused at source
  if (rst) gnt <= '0; else gnt <= pick;
logic u;
always_ff @(posedge clk) u <= u;           // never loaded, and read: refused at score
assign sel = !u;
always_ff @(posedge clk) q <= a / b;       // a run-time divisor that reads a signal: refused at clocked_rules
```

## Task authors: `task.json`

Mistakes in a task definition fail loudly so a typo cannot silently change the vector budget or the banlist.

| refused | why | state |
|---|---|---|
| **task.json banlist naming an operator outside + - * / % ****<br>e.g. "banlist": {"operators": ["<<"]} | Only the six arithmetic operators have a Yosys cell map and a slang operator map. The CLI `banlist.py --ban '<<'` dies with a KeyError traceback instead of the clean message. | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: a task that needs it (barrel shifter bans << >> <<< >>>; a comparator bans < > <= >=), then OP_CELLS and _binop_symbol extended with $shl $shr $sshl $sshr $lt $le $gt $ge [BANOPS] |
| **task.json with unknown keys, bad postsynth corners, a status other than ready/draft**<br>e.g. a typo in a postsynth key; corners naming a non-input port; a ready task without a proved reference | Schema discipline: typos must not silently change the vector budget. | **refused-now** |

What is refused:

```systemverilog
"banlist": {"operators": ["<<"]}     // unknown operator
"allow_bv_decide": true                  // an infrastructure error: no external solvers
```

## Constructs the ls-sv tier refuses, as seen from svGolf

The `extract` and `design` stages pass on the refusals of the language tier (ls-sv). The full register is `docs/sv-refusals.md` in the lean-surfaces repository; the ones a task is most likely to run into, with what has to exist before each is allowed:

| construct | why you might want it | prerequisite |
|---|---|---|
| `CallExpression ($countones, $onehot, $left, array and enum methods)` | $countones and one-hot predicates for fixed-width packed signals (the banlist already treats these bit queries as +) | none for fixed-width `$countones`, `$onehot`, `$onehot0`, and numeric enum methods; proposed prerequisite: per-built-in lowering for parameter-dependent widths, `$left`, enum `name()`, and array methods |
| `ConditionalStatement:Unique \| :Unique0 \| :Priority` | unique / priority in priority encoders and one-hot muxes | a violated unique / unique0 / priority claim becomes a run-time error on the settled state, forced by Terminates2 |
| `ConversionExpression:Explicit` | casts to a parameter width such as `N'(x)` (a cast to a fixed width such as `8'(x)` loads) | per-point width and signedness rules for parameter-named and aggregate casts |
| `ConversionExpression:width` | `$signed(x)` widened into a wider sum, the usual way to sign-extend; meanwhile sign-extend by hand: `{{K{x[W-1]}}, x}` | none recorded; proposed prerequisite: symbolic SignedResize for signed operands |
| `SimpleAssignmentPatternExpression \| StructuredAssignmentPatternExpression \| ReplicatedAssignmentPatternExpression` | lookup tables and constants written as `'{...}` patterns | symbolic assignment patterns for parameter-dependent, unpacked and effectful aggregate shapes |
| `InsideExpression, ValueRangeExpression` | range checks (`a inside {[3:5]}`) in decoders (the pinned Yosys 0.53 cannot read `inside` either) | point-dependent membership widths and a four-state simulator oracle for the remaining symbolic forms |
| `instance hierarchy deeper than its module library (recursive instantiation)` | recursive instantiation: bitonic sort, Karatsuba | flattening by induction in Hier2 / Hier2Gen with a symbolic recursion depth (bitonic sort, Karatsuba) |
| `PrimitiveInstanceSymbol:PrimitiveInstance` | built-in gate primitives (`and g1(y, a, b)`) for gate-level golf | none recorded; proposed prerequisite: built-in gate primitives first; UDP tables have no recorded plan |
| x, z or ? digits in a literal outside a casez/casex item wildcard | don't-care assignments (`'x`) to save area, via the x-taint feature | the x-taint feature: allow x sources but forbid x-tainted values from reaching non-monotone decisions; first measure the area gain of don't-cares on a real task |

And what ls-sv will not model and svGolf will not accept for as long as the tools disagree or the construct is not hardware:

- Anything the PIPELINE tools read differently (slang and ls-sv for the proof, Yosys for the score, Verilator and Xcelium as simulators; `P-NO-SILENT-PICK`, and `P-SAME-PROGRAM` where Yosys differs from slang): narrow net actuals into wider net inputs, partly out-of-range part selects, bit-select indexes wider than 32 bits, context-width port actuals, instance-parameter overrides evaluated at different widths, initialized variables with a second writer, the hex string escape `\xHH` (Yosys and Xcelium read the letter x; the named control escapes `\a \v \f` are admitted since 2026-11-01, Xcelium alone differs), self-reading `always_comb` (the event-driven simulators against the synthesizers). A difference that only Icarus (or only Xcelium, against LRM text the others follow) shows is a declared departure, not a refusal.
- Programs slang rejects (`P-SAME-PROGRAM`; what the slang driver reports: parse and elaboration errors always, analysis errors too since 2026-11-01 (the banlist front check and the fourstate stage read them), with what is still unread listed under 'limits'): undeclared names, two writers of one bit when one of them is `always_comb`/`always_ff`, writing an input port, an undefined module, an `always` without timing control. Yosys alone would accept several of them silently.
- Tool directives of any kind (`P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES`): `ifdef SYNTHESIS, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments.
- Delays, timing and randomness in a combinational task (`P-NO-TIME`, `P-DETERMINISM`); non-hardware constructs such as classes, strings, reals, dynamic memory and `fork`/`join` (`P-SYNTHESIZABLE`: out of scope while the scored frontend is Yosys `read_verilog -sv`). Host access (reading files, system calls, DPI) is disallowed by its own policy (decided 2026-10-31).
- Anything that lets a submission change what the checker trusts (`P-TRUSTED-BASE`): `sorry`, user axioms, `extern` / `implemented_by`, a player-supplied envelope.
- Anything in the SystemVerilog text that reaches the machine the checker runs on (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`; the Lean file is not covered, see the limits): `$readmemh` / `$readmemb` / `$writemem*`, `$fopen` and the file I/O family, `$system`, `$test$plusargs` / `$value$plusargs`, dump writers (`$dumpfile`, ...), DPI imports and exports, and escaped `$`-names that Yosys reads as system tasks.

## How a refusal becomes allowed

- Every refusal above has a state. `refused-now` means no change is planned. `later` names the prerequisite that has to exist first; when it exists, the refusal is lifted by a pull request.
- **How to propose it.** Open a pull request against Proglib that adds the feature to ls-sv (extractor, `LeanModels/Sv`), with differential cases against independent oracles (Xcelium pinned data, Icarus, Verilator, Yosys): a disagreement is fixed or declared, never ignored. The maintainers approve every such PR.
- **If the construct brings an x source** (a function local read before assignment, a latch that is never loaded, `always @*`), a rule in `score/fourstate.py` must land first or in the same PR; the post-synthesis check is the backstop, not the plan.
- **For the checker's own rules** (the source gate, the banlist, the statement), changing a refusal changes what every earlier submission means: the PR must say so, and leaderboard entries record the Proglib revision they were checked against.
- **Update the register.** Add or edit the row in `docs/sv-refusals.json`, run `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --write`, and `--check` must pass.

## Known limits (not refusals)

- The post-synthesis check is sampling (fixed corners, task corners, harvested comparison constants, seeded random): a difference confined to a region no comparison constant selects can pass (`oob_rare.sv`, `zpair_add_rare.sv` pass it alone; the static rules are the only line there).
- The Lean file is not scanned for host access (`#eval`, `IO`, `run_cmd`, `elab`, `initialize`, `unsafe`; `import Lean` is allowed), because a scan cannot stop it: every process that runs submitted text (the Lean compiles, the comparator and `leanchecker`, the extractor, Yosys, Verilator and the compiled model) runs inside the checker's sandbox instead (svGolf's README.md, "Sandbox": no network, reads of its own inputs only, one output directory, no other program, an allowlisted environment). `check.py --sandbox require`, what every competition run uses, refuses to run without it; the default `auto` runs without it, and says so, where the mechanism is missing; on Linux it is not yet checked end to end with Lean (2026-11-10). Measured 2026-10-31, before the sandbox: a reference Solution.lean with an added `#eval IO.FS.readFile "/etc/hosts"` and an `IO.FS.writeFile` was accepted and did both, which is why the host-access refusals of the SystemVerilog text (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`) are not enough for the Lean file.
- The parameter's declared type is not pinned by the statement; the multi-point cross-check at the scoring point keeps the scored design one ls-sv and slang agree on, elsewhere the statement is about ls-sv's reading.
- The banlist front check is heuristic (a variable copied from a loop counter counts as run-time); the Yosys backstop covers the scored points only.
- The fourstate stage checks the points the checker probes, no others (since 2026-11-06 the scoring point, then the task's probe and backstop points; before, the scoring point only), and filters `tri-state` warnings out of Yosys `check`. Its run-time index rule reasons from index TYPES: `a[i-1]` with a 2-bit `i` is a 32-bit index and is refused on any declared range (over-refusal), as is any procedural loop counter used as an index.
- A gate hole not yet measured: x/z digits are exempt anywhere inside a casez/casex item EXPRESSION, not only as the item's own literal (`casez (a[1:0]) (a[0] == 1'bz) ? 2'b00 : 2'b01: ...` passes the gate). Whether ls-sv and Yosys then differ was not measured; do not rely on it.
- A plain syntax error is reported by the gate as `preprocessor-skipped text` before the extractor or Yosys see it; `always @(*)` passes the gate (the `(*)` is exempt), and ls-sv runs it as `always_comb` only under the lowering rules of Proglib's `docs/sv-proc-lowering.md` (a block that assigns a variable on some paths only is refused at `design`).
- `ARITH_PRIMITIVES` (`$alu $macc $macc_v2 $lcu $fa`) cannot be instantiated by a submission: the backstop reads without `-icells`, so instantiating one fails earlier with `yosys failed`. In a task that bans `+` or `-` the same five types are what the post-`alumacc` check rejects: every one that `alumacc` builds, e.g. for a run-time ordering comparison (`sg-ban-cmp`, decided 2026-11-05).
- `--no-gate` in `score.py` and `postsynth.py` is a research flag: the result says `gated: false` and is not a svGolf score. Missing Verilator, make, a C++ compiler, Yosys or `svgolf-eval` is an infrastructure error (exit 2), never a rejection.
- The ordering-comparison rule (`sg-ban-cmp`) is the backstop's alone, so it holds at the backstop points only: a run-time comparison in code that only other parameter values elaborate (measured: a generate branch taken only at `N = 7` in `add`) passes the banlist, where a `+` in the same place is rejected by the front check. The scored netlist never contains it.
- slang's ANALYSIS-pass errors (`multiple-always-assigns`, `mixed-var-assigns`, `multiple-cont-assigns`, "cannot assign to input port", "'always' procedure does not advance time") are read since 2026-11-01 by the banlist front check and the `fourstate` stage (`score/slangdriver.py`, the Driver's own severities, per parameter point) and by the extractor. Still unread: the elaboration warnings the driver promotes to errors (`IndexOOB`, `RangeOOB`, ...: `fourstate`'s rule (c) refuses the out-of-range ones as x sources); a module the design does not instantiate (docs/sv-refusals.json, `holes`). The banlist front check runs for every task: every task bans run-time `/ % **` since 2026-11-06, so none has an empty banlist (until then such a task skipped the front check, and `fourstate` was the only stage that read the analysis errors there).
